themes_detail.label: Industrial Waste Surge
themes_detail.summary: Industrial waste complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting either a new industrial operation, illegal dumping, or enforcement crackdown in East New York/Cypress Hills.
evidence: 3 industrial waste complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks prior (2300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically extreme anomaly
Timing suggests sudden onset rather than chronic problem
reporting_angles: Identify the source: Is a specific facility or illegal dumping operation behind the spike?
Interview residents near complaint hotspots about exposure and health concerns

themes_detail.label: House of Worship Noise Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from houses of worship jumped to 8 LAST WEEK versus 0.9 weekly average over 8 weeks—an 814% spike (z-score: 5.23)—indicating either amplified activity, new enforcement, or community friction around religious institutions in the district.
evidence: 8 noise complaints from houses of worship LAST WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over 8 weeks prior (814% increase)
Pattern suggests either event-driven spike or new community sensitivity to noise
reporting_angles: Which houses of worship are generating complaints, and what activities triggered them?
Interview residents and faith leaders about tensions over hours, amplification, or frequency of services

themes_detail.label: Building Inspection Authority Surge
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints quadrupled to 4 THIS WEEK from 0.8 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 433% spike (z-score: 4.91)—suggesting either increased code violations, an active inspection sweep, or landlord non-compliance in a specific area.
evidence: 4 SPIT complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% spike)
Z-score of 4.91 indicates strong statistical signal
525 building permits filed in 90 days (334 alterations) suggests active construction/renovation activity that may trigger inspections
reporting_angles: Is DOB conducting a targeted inspection campaign in specific neighborhoods or building types?
What violations are SPIT finding and how do they correlate with recent DOB permit filings?

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Missing street signs surged to 15 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO from a 5.9 weekly average—a 155% increase (z-score: 4.64)—while dead/dying trees spiked to 6 complaints LAST WEEK from 1.1 baseline, suggesting deferred or poor maintenance across public infrastructure.
evidence: 15 missing street sign complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 5.9 weekly average (155% spike, z-score: 4.64)
6 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (433% spike, z-score: 4.63)
Convergence of two separate infrastructure maintenance issues suggests resource or management gaps
reporting_angles: Has the Parks Department or DOT reduced maintenance crews or shifted priorities in CD305?
Conduct a street-by-street survey of signage and tree conditions in the most affected neighborhoods

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Spike (Multi-Category)
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints across multiple categories surged 3 WEEKS AGO: street/sidewalk noise hit 63 complaints (234% above 18.9 weekly average) and general noise complaints reached 36 (116% above 16.6 average), suggesting either a major event, event venue activity, or cumulative community frustration.
evidence: 63 street/sidewalk noise complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 18.9 weekly average (234% spike, z-score: 3.86)
36 general noise complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 16.6 weekly average (116% increase, z-score: 3.65)
Residential noise also elevated at 2,319 complaints over 90 days, indicating chronic baseline problem
reporting_angles: Was there a specific event (concert, festival, construction project) 3 weeks ago that triggered the spike?
Interview residents about whether noise levels have normalized since or remain elevated
